title: What does it mean to be a developer now?
author: TheGamingSpringbok
selftext:
One of the biggest game technology companies in the world is openly acknowledging that its engineers aren't manually writing most of their code anymore.

Thats Epic Games. And Epic isn't alone.

NetEase, another massive gaming company behind titles like Marvel Rivals and Where Winds Meet, has also confirmed that AI is integrated into its programming, art, design, and QA workflows. Its internal coding tools have evolved beyond simple autocomplete to handling entire development tasks.

And honestly, I don't think indie teams and solo developers are exceptions to this trend either.

SO what does it mean to be a developer now if most of the code is no longer manually done?

comments.author: StoneCypher
comments.body: it means tolerating a bunch of neckbeard juniors trying to write meaningless wisdom posts in subs that want to be dev subs but can’t be because of all the meaningless wisdom posts

replies.body: since this is gamedev sub I want to mention my friend that vibecoded his game on godot and the agents made a godfile with over 75k lines and I didnt even knew that was possible

replies.author: StoneCypher
replies.body: why would that not be possible?

replies.author: I_Rarely_Jump
replies.body:
I assume they mean "possible to vibe code that badly".

I also wonder what model would structure code like that, as in my experience most models are pretty good at project structure, you'd have to explicitly ask for it to make a godfile

replies.author: StoneCypher
replies.body:
i’m uncertain why you think it’s a problem 

it wasn’t even really a problem back when humans read the code

complaining about file length is one of those classic things that immediately tells you that the senior engineer you’re talking to has never worked on regular commercial software 

turbotax has a dozen files over a million lines each

replies.author: Morpegom
replies.body:
oh sorry mister senior bazillion dev, since you know a lot about programming, you should know that "godfile" doesnt mean "bigfile", it means "the file that does everything"

and yes, it is bad, commercial software is different on its own way, and even being different it is still bad to work with agents

it increases by a lot the cost of reading or editing the file when using agents (you are on a AI sub, just to remember), editing gets ambiguous and the parallel agents conflicts on the same file

turbo tax just proves that companys can survive on legacy code, it doesnt mean that it is a good thing or should happen

replies.author: StoneCypher
replies.body:
(checks watch)

i wasn’t sarcastic to you but ok

replies.author: I_Rarely_Jump
replies.body:
> turbotax has a dozen files over a million lines each 

Uh, you sure those aren't just generated files...? Like the files created by the build or something?

There is 0 reason to put so much code in a single file, there are no benefits at all, only drawbacks (like your IDE shitting the bed by trying to parse a ridiculous amount of code).

replies.author: Morpegom
replies.body:
idk, i've been working on personal projects for years, and my games started breaking after 20k lines or so, until I learned about godfiles

not saying that the game wouldnt work, but agents have a context window that fills pretty quickly, opus itself advises that no file should go over 10k lines because its very likely that he will break a lot when fixing something

so I imagine the damage of what 75k of lines on a single file can do

comments.author: Dicethrower
comments.body: A developer's job is to ship games. The means through which that is accomplished changed. The job is the same.

comments.author: Morpegom
comments.body:
A film director doesn’t hold the camera, act, edit, or score the movie. Nobody asks “what does it mean to be a director if they don’t do any of it by hand?” because the job is knowin what the film should be, rejecting the bad takes, and owning the result. It says “A Hideo Kojima Game” on the box and he probably didnt touched anything on the game itself.

You are probably a young teenager or a entitlted adult, no hate from my part, you just need to know that we have been there before. In the 50s people had to type the machine code itself by hand, years later compilers did this automatically, so you didnt had to learn assembly anymore.

comments.author: Ok-Foundation-8006
comments.body: Getting tired of all these labels to make people feel special about themselves. I think we are transitioning from “I’m a dev” to “I make games”. The goals are still the same, the barrier to entry and the path to get there has changed. I’m saying this as someone who has worn a bunch of hats over the last decade.
